findings: Left bundle branch block in advanced disease
Low limb lead voltage with poor R progression

echoTasks.find: Moderately dilated left ventricle with globally reduced thickening
Functional mitral regurgitation from tethering with an enlarged left atrium
Dilated thin walled ventricle with poor systolic thickening in long axis

auscultation.murmur: Soft pansystolic murmur of functional mitral regurgitation

exam.general: Young mother 3 months after delivery, breathless on housework, mild ankle oedema
exam.other: Baby thriving on formula, mother anxious about breastfeeding on drugs
exam.precordium: Displaced apex beat in the sixth space
exam.pulse: Regular 88, normal volume, narrow pulse pressure

history.a: Breathlessness since the last month of pregnancy, worsened after a normal delivery 3 months ago
Orthopnoea with two pillows, no paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea
No hypertension, no diabetes, no prior heart disease
No alcohol, no smoking, vegetarian diet
Takes no cardiac drugs yet, iron continued
First child, family supportive, worried about caring for the baby

keyPoints: Confirm peripartum cardiomyopathy with exclusion of ischaemia, thyroid disease and anaemia
Start guideline directed therapy compatible with breastfeeding choices, per the ESC heart failure and pregnancy guidance
Add bromocriptine discussion at a referral centre where the protocol supports it
Plan contraception counselling before discharge, as recurrence risk in later pregnancy is high
Schedule 6 monthly echo to document recovery or persistence before device decisions
management.model: Heart failure therapy adapted to the postpartum period with cause exclusion, contraception planning, and recovery tracking

sources: ESC guideline on heart failure, in own words
ESC guidance on cardiovascular disease in pregnancy, in own words
stem: A 41 year old woman from Surat, 3 months after a normal delivery, reports progressive breathlessness since late pregnancy with orthopnoea and ankle oedema. The apex is displaced with a third sound gallop.
teaching: Peripartum cardiomyopathy is new systolic failure in late pregnancy or early postpartum months
Moderate means EF 30 to 40 percent with moderate dilatation
Fellow quantification adds diastolic grade, filling pressure and recovery tracking
Therapy must balance guideline pillars against breastfeeding choices with contraception planned
title: Peripartum dilated cardiomyopathy with moderate dysfunction
